title: Sarga Twenty — verses 1–49
html:
Title of the sarga: none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga (iti śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-caritāmṛte mahākāvye śrīla-karṇapūra-kṛtau viṁśatitamaḥ sargaḥ, "Thus [ends] the twentieth sarga in the great poem Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita, the work of Srila Karnapura"; it goes on: "This great poem Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita is complete. Number of verses: 1911"). Metre: - 1–36 and 41 — śālinī (ma-ta-ta-ga-ga: — — — — | — ⏑ — — ⏑ — —; 11 syllables per pada, caesura after the fourth). The edition says: "up to verse 36 — śālinī". - 37 and 47 — śārdūla-vikrīḍita (ma-sa-ja-sa-ta-ta-ga: ———⏑⏑—⏑—⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑—; 19 syllables per pada). - 38–39 and 48 — mandākrāntā (ma-bha-na-ta-ta-ga-ga: ————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑——⏑——; 17 syllables per pada). - 40 — śikhariṇī (ya-ma-na-sa-bha-la-ga: ⏑—————⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑——⏑⏑⏑—; 17 syllables per pada). - 42–45 and 49 — vasantatilakā (ta-bha-ja-ja-ga-ga: ——⏑—⏑⏑⏑—⏑⏑—⏑——; 14 syllables per pada). - 46 — mālinī (na-na-ma-ya-ya: ⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑⏑———⏑——⏑——; 15 syllables per pada, caesura after the eighth).

Total verses: 49. The publisher gives the total number of verses of the poem as 1911 (in the colophon and in his note after verse 49). The printed numbering of the twenty sargas runs without gaps or repetitions and adds up to 1912 (29 + 122 + 144 + 77 + 129 + 123 + 107 + 63 + 95 + 80 + 89 + 134 + 148 + 135 + 110 + 49 + 66 + 63 + 100 + 49); the difference of one is not explained by the numbering itself and is presumably a slip in the publisher's count (his other figures in the same note are also inexact; see the note on 49). The unnumbered quotations in Sargas 6 and 7 are not included in either figure.

Contents of the passage: the journey through Bengal, the return, the Lord's departure; the author's conclusion. - 1–10 — the Lord dismisses the ministers; by Prataparudra's order houses are built for Him everywhere; crowds of people; the Lord and Puri point each other out (7); Ramananda turns back from Bhadra (9). - 11–19 — Gauda: the abode of Raghava (12); the house of Srivasa and the crowds; the secret departure by boat at night; Srivasa and the others search for Him. - 20–25 — Shantipura: the meeting with Advaita; Mother Shachi (23); six days; Advaita regales the people. - 26–30 — a place across the Ganga, west of Navadvipa (Kuliya?); crowds; the Lord hides Himself. - 31–36 — an obscure place, "Gopinatha" (31); the way towards the Yamuna, the return to the Ganga, then to Puri (32–34); the second departure for the Yamuna (35); Ramananda gives up his life in separation (36 — at variance with the Chaitanya-charitamrita). - 37–41 — summary: twenty years of festivals in Puri; the Lord's departure to His own abode; chronology: sannyasa in His twenty-fourth year, three years of wandering, twenty years in Puri, forty-seven years in all (40–41). - 42–49 — the author's conclusion: - the source — the records of Murari (Gupta), which "the child saw" (42–43); - a blessing on the poem; the author's humility (44–45, 48); - the signature: the youngest son of Shivananda Sena (46); - the hero of the poem is dhīrodātta (47); - the date of completion: Shaka 1464 (1542 CE), the month of Ashadha, a Monday, the second tithi of the dark fortnight (49).

Verse 1

रात्रिर्याता नाथ तल्पं जहीही-
त्याकर्ण्य पक्षिणां कूजितानि ।
नेत्रे निद्रामुद्रिते जागृहीति
द्रागाक्षिप्यन् पाणिनाथोदियाय ॥१॥

rātrir yātā nātha talpaṁ jahīhīty
ākarṇya pakṣiṇāṁ kūjitāni |
netre nidrā-mudrite jāgṛhīti
drāg ākṣipyan pāṇinā thodiyāya (pāṇinātha udiyāya) ||1||

rātriḥ — the night; yātā — has gone; nātha — O Master; talpam — the bed; jahīhi — leave; iti — thus; ākarṇya — having heard; pakṣiṇām — of the birds; kūjitāni — the warbling; netre — [His] two eyes; nidrā — by sleep; mudrite — sealed; jāgṛhi — wake up; iti — [saying] thus; drāk — quickly; ākṣipyan — rubbing; pāṇinā — with [His] hand; atha — then; udiyāya — rose.

1Hearing the warbling of the birds — "The night has gone, O Master; leave Your bed!" — He quickly rubbed with His hand His eyes, sealed by sleep, [saying to them,] "Wake up!", and then rose.

Note. The metre is śālinī (so the edition: "up to verse 36 — śālinī"). As printed, the second pada has only ten syllables (ākarṇya pakṣiṇāṁ kūjitāni: — — ⏑ — ⏑ — — ⏑ — ⏑): of the four heavy syllables of the opening only three are present, and -ṇya is light; something has dropped out. The printed run pāṇināthodiyāya is to be divided pāṇinā atha udiyāya, "with the hand; then [He] rose"; the division pāṇinā thodiyāya in the transliteration line is merely mechanical.

Verse 2

निर्माल्यान्नं तत्र सद्यः समेतं
दृष्ट्वा हर्षादाह्निकान्यारभेत ।
अन्नं पानं पिष्टकादि प्रकामं
तैस्तैर्भुक्त्वा प्रीतिमांश्च प्रतस्थे ॥२॥

nirmālyānnaṁ tatra sadyaḥ sametaṁ
dṛṣṭvā harṣād āhnikāny ārabheta |
annaṁ pānaṁ piṣṭakādi prakāmaṁ
tais tair bhuktvā prītimāṁś ca pratasthe ||2||

nirmālya — sanctified; annam — food; tatra — there; sadyaḥ — just; sametam — arrived; dṛṣṭvā — having seen; harṣāt — joyfully; āhnikāni — the daily rites; ārabheta — began; annam — rice; pānam — drink; piṣṭaka-ādi — cakes and the rest; prakāmam — to [His] heart's content; taiḥ taiḥ — with all of them; bhuktvā — having eaten; prītimān — pleased; ca — and; pratasthe — set out.

2Seeing the sanctified food that had just arrived there, He joyfully began His daily rites; and having eaten to His heart's content, with all of them, rice, drink, cakes and the rest, He set out, pleased.

Note. The optative ārabheta is used in the sense of the past (for the metre).

Verse 3

तत्रामात्यौ तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टौ
ताभ्यां भूयो नेत्रपाथोजपाथः ।
तेने क्षामे तत्तनू हन्त ताभ्या-
मुत्साहोऽयं कः प्रकारो विधातुः ॥३॥

tatrāmātyau tena samyag visṛṣṭau
tābhyāṁ bhūyo netra-pāthoja-pāthaḥ |
tene kṣāme tat-tanū hanta tābhyām
utsāho 'yaṁ kaḥ prakāro vidhātuḥ ||3||

tatra — there; amātyau — the two ministers; tena — by Him; samyak — duly; visṛṣṭau — [were] dismissed; tābhyām — by the two; bhūyaḥ — abundantly; netra — of the eyes; pāthoja — of the lotuses; pāthaḥ — the water; tene — was shed; kṣāme — [became] wasted; tat — their; tanū — two bodies; hanta — alas; tābhyām — by the two [had been shown]; utsāhaḥ — zeal; ayam — this; kaḥ — what; prakāraḥ — [is] the way; vidhātuḥ — of the Creator.

3There the two ministers were duly dismissed by Him. They shed abundant water from the lotuses of their eyes, and their bodies — alas! — wasted away; and such zeal [had been shown] by them! What a way the Creator has!

Note. The ministers are Mangaraja and Harichandana (19.94).

Verse 4

देशं देशं प्रत्युपेयुः समन्ता-
दाज्ञा राज्ञो लेखपूर्वाः समस्ताः ।
स्थाने स्थाने नव्यनव्यं निशान्तं
सामग्रीभिः कर्त्तुमग्रे पवित्रम् ॥४॥

deśaṁ deśaṁ pratyupeyuḥ samantād
ājñā rājño lekha-pūrvāḥ samastāḥ |
sthāne sthāne navya-navyaṁ niśāntaṁ
sāmagrībhiḥ karttum agre pavitram ||4||

deśam deśam — to land after land; pratyupeyuḥ — came; samantāt — on every side; ājñāḥ — the orders; rājñaḥ — of the king; lekha-pūrvāḥ — written; samastāḥ — all; sthāne sthāne — at every place; navya-navyam — brand-new; niśāntam — a dwelling; sāmagrībhiḥ — with provisions; karttum — to make; agre — in advance; pavitram — clean.

4To land after land, on every side, came all the king's written orders: at every place a brand-new, clean dwelling was to be made ready in advance, with provisions.

Verse 5

उद्यन्नासीद्यत्र तैरेष नाथो
हर्षोत्कर्षाल्लक्षसंख्यैर्मनुष्यैः ।
निष्प्रत्यूहं तत्र तत्रेक्षणाब्जैः
काकुप्रोक्तैः पूजितः संस्तुतश्च ॥५॥

udyann āsīd yatra tair eṣa nātho
harṣotkarṣāl lakṣa-saṅkhyair manuṣyaiḥ |
niṣpratyūhaṁ tatra tatrekṣaṇābjaiḥ
kāku-proktaiḥ pūjitaḥ saṁstutaś ca ||5||

udyan — appearing; āsīt — was; yatra — wherever; taiḥ — by those; eṣaḥ — this; nāthaḥ — Master; harṣa — of joy; utkarṣāt — from the excess; lakṣa — in hundreds of thousands; saṅkhyaiḥ — numbering; manuṣyaiḥ — by people; niṣpratyūham — without hindrance; tatra tatra — there; īkṣaṇa — of the eyes; abjaiḥ — with the lotuses; kāku — plaintive; proktaiḥ — with words; pūjitaḥ — [was] worshipped; saṁstutaḥ — praised; ca — and.

5Wherever this Master appeared, there, out of the excess of their joy, people numbering hundreds of thousands worshipped Him without hindrance with the lotuses of their eyes and praised Him with plaintive words.

Verse 6

अद्य श्वो वा नूनमत्रैष्यतीति
प्रोच्चैरासीदग्रतो हर्षनादः ।
पश्चादायातीति तस्मादुपेतो
भो भोः पश्चादेव सर्वत्र भूयः ॥६॥

adya śvo vā nūnam atraiṣyatīti
proccair āsīd agrato harṣa-nādaḥ |
paścād āyātīti tasmād upeto
bho bhoḥ paścād eva sarvatra bhūyaḥ ||6||

adya — today; śvaḥ — tomorrow; vā — or; nūnam — surely; atra — here; eṣyati — He will come; iti — thus; pra-uccaiḥ — very loudly; āsīt — there was; agrataḥ — ahead; harṣa — of joy; nādaḥ — a cry; paścāt — afterwards; āyāti — He is coming; iti — thus; tasmāt — then; upetaḥ — He has come; bho bhoḥ — ho, ho!; paścāt eva — afterwards; sarvatra — everywhere; bhūyaḥ — again.

6"Today or tomorrow He will surely come here!" — such was the cry of joy that rang out very loudly ahead [of Him]; afterwards, "He is coming!"; then, "Ho, ho! He has come!" — and so again everywhere afterwards.

Verse 7

केचित् केचित्तत्र पप्रच्छुरार्य्याः
क्वासौ क्वासौ कृष्णचैतन्यचन्द्रः ।
इत्थं नाथं पूरिणं तं प्रभुं तं
तावन्योन्यं दर्शयामासतुस्तान् ॥७॥

kecit kecit tatra papracchur āryāḥ
kvāsau kvāsau kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ |
itthaṁ nāthaṁ pūriṇaṁ taṁ prabhuṁ taṁ
tāv anyonyaṁ darśayāmāsatus tān ||7||

kecit kecit — some; tatra — there; papracchuḥ — asked; āryāḥ — worthy [people]; kva asau — where is He; kṛṣṇa-caitanya-candraḥ — Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra; ittham — thus; nātham — the Master; pūriṇam — Puri; tam — that; prabhum — Lord; tam — that; tau — the two; anyonyam — each other; darśayāmāsatuḥ — pointed out; tān — to them.

7Some worthy people there asked: "Where is He, where is He — Krishna-Chaitanya-chandra?" Thereupon those two pointed each other out to them: [Puri showed them] the Master, that Lord, [and the Lord showed them] that Puri.

Note. A playful scene: each of the two points to the other. Puri is presumably Paramananda Puri, the Lord's companion on this journey (19.6, 12). There is no such scene in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16).

Verse 8

वासं वासं प्रत्युपेते प्रभाते
राज्ञामाज्ञायन्त्रिताः सर्व एव ।
देशे देशे शुद्धगेहानि कृत्वा
सामग्रीश्च प्रोन्मदा आनयन्ति ॥८॥

vāsaṁ vāsaṁ pratyupete prabhāte
rājñām ājñā-yantritāḥ sarva eva |
deśe deśe śuddha-gehāni kṛtvā
sāmagrīś ca pronmadā ānayanti ||8||

vāsam vāsam — at halting place after halting place; pratyupete — when [He] had arrived; prabhāte — at dawn; rājñām — of the kings; ājñā — by the order; yantritāḥ — constrained; sarve eva — all; deśe deśe — in every land; śuddha — clean; gehāni — houses; kṛtvā — having built; sāmagrīḥ — provisions; ca — and; pronmadāḥ — in rapture; ānayanti — bring.

8Whenever He arrived at dawn at one halting place after another, all [the people] in every land, bound by the order of the kings, built clean houses and in rapture brought provisions.

Note. Rājñām is plural, "of the kings"; perhaps it stands for rājño, "of the king".

Verse 9

रामानन्दो भद्रपर्यन्तमेत्य
प्रत्यावृत्तस्तेन सम्यग्विसृष्टः ।
विच्छेदार्त्तः क्षेत्रमेव प्रतस्थे
गौराङ्गोऽयं सोऽप्युपेयादुदीचीम् ॥९॥

rāmānando bhadra-paryantam etya
pratyāvṛttas tena samyag visṛṣṭaḥ |
vicchedārttaḥ kṣetram eva pratasthe
gaurāṅgo 'yaṁ so 'py upeyād udīcīm ||9||

rāmānandaḥ — Ramananda; bhadra-paryantam — as far as Bhadra; etya — having come; pratyāvṛttaḥ — turned back; tena — by Him; samyak — duly; visṛṣṭaḥ — dismissed; viccheda — by separation; ārttaḥ — afflicted; kṣetram eva — to [Sri] Kshetra; pratasthe — set out; gaurāṅgaḥ ayam — and this Gauranga; saḥ api — He for His part; upeyāt — went; udīcīm — to the north.

9Ramananda, having come as far as Bhadra and been duly dismissed by Him, turned back and, afflicted by separation, set out for [Sri] Kshetra; and Gauranga for His part went on to the north.

Note. Bhadra is Bhadraka. According to the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 16.151–155), Ramananda accompanies the Lord as far as Remuna, and there, taking leave, falls unconscious.

Verse 10

ओड्रं यावद्भूपतेर्लेखयुक्ता
आसंस्तावत्तावदेवं धुरीणैः ।
प्रातर्धूपान्तर्गतं राजयोग्यं
निर्माल्यं चानीतमेव प्रकामम् ॥१०॥

oḍraṁ yāvad bhūpater lekha-yuktā
āsaṁs tāvat tāvad evaṁ dhurīṇaiḥ |
prātar-dhūpāntargataṁ rāja-yogyaṁ
nirmālyaṁ cānītam eva prakāmam ||10||

oḍram yāvat — as far as Odra [extended]; bhūpateḥ — of the king; lekha — with the letters; yuktāḥ — provided; āsan — [the places] were; tāvat tāvat — so far, all the way; evam — thus; dhurīṇaiḥ — by the officials in charge; prātaḥ — of the morning; dhūpa — dhupa [offering]; antargatam — forming part; rāja-yogyam — fit for a king; nirmālyam — the sanctified remnants; ca — and; ānītam eva — were brought; prakāmam — in abundance.

10As far as Odra [extended], [the places] were provided with the king's letters; and all that way the officials in charge thus brought in abundance the sanctified remnants of the morning dhupa offering, fit for a king.

Note. Odra is Orissa.

Verse 11

श्रीमान् गौडं देशमासाद्य गङ्गा
द्रष्टव्येति प्रेमवैह्वल्यनुन्नः ।
तत्संसृष्टिस्निग्धमुग्धान्तरात्मा
तत्तत्स्थानाप्यायिताङ्गः स रेजे ॥११॥

śrīmān gauḍaṁ deśam āsādya gaṅgā
draṣṭavyeti prema-vaihvalya-nunnaḥ |
tat-saṁsṛṣṭi-snigdha-mugdhāntarātmā
tat-tat-sthānāpyāyitāṅgaḥ sa reje ||11||

śrīmān — the beautiful [Lord]; gauḍam — of Gauda; deśam — the land; āsādya — having reached; gaṅgā — the Ganga; draṣṭavyā — must be seen; iti — thus; prema — of love; vaihvalya — by the agitation; nunnaḥ — impelled; tat — with her; saṁsṛṣṭi — by contact; snigdha — softened; mugdha — [and] charmed; antara-ātmā — [whose] inner self [was]; tat-tat — of those various; sthāna — places; āpyāyita — refreshed; aṅgaḥ — [whose] limbs [were]; saḥ — He; reje — shone.

11Having reached the land of Gauda, the beautiful [Lord], impelled by the agitation of love — "The Ganga must be seen!" — shone, His inner self softened and charmed by contact with her, His limbs refreshed by those various places.

Note. Gauda is Bengal. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 12

आगत्य श्रीराघवस्याश्रमान्तः
श्रीगौरश्चन्द्रवत् पूर्वशैलम् ।
गन्धैर्माल्यैः पुष्पधूपोपहारैः
प्रेमाविष्टः कौतुकी संममाद ॥१२॥

āgatya śrī-rāghavasyāśramāntaḥ
śrī-gauraś candravat pūrva-śailam |
gandhair mālyaiḥ puṣpa-dhūpopahāraiḥ
premāviṣṭaḥ kautukī saṁmamāda ||12||

āgatya — having come; śrī-rāghavasya — of Sri Raghava; āśrama — the abode; antaḥ — into; śrī-gauraḥ — Sri Gaura; candra-vat — like the moon; pūrva-śailam — [to] the Eastern Mountain; gandhaiḥ — with fragrances; mālyaiḥ — with garlands; puṣpa — flowers; dhūpa — incense; upahāraiḥ — [and] offerings; prema — by love; āviṣṭaḥ — possessed; kautukī — delighted; saṁmamāda — rejoiced.

12Having come into the abode of Sri Raghava, as the moon [comes] to the Eastern Mountain, Sri Gaura, possessed by love and delighted, rejoiced amid fragrances, garlands, flowers, incense and offerings.

Note. Raghava Pandita of Panihati (cf. the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 16.202–205: the Lord arrives at Panihati by boat, and Raghava Pandita leads Him with difficulty through the crowd to his house). As printed, the second pada has only ten syllables (śrī-gauraś candravat pūrva-śailam: — — — — ⏑ — — ⏑ — ⏑): of the five heavy syllables of the opening only four are present.

Verse 13

तत्र स्थित्वा राघवस्याश्रमेऽसौ
नीत्वा नाथः पञ्चषान् वासरान् सः ।
ज्येष्ठं तावच्छ्रीनवद्वीपभूमा-
वग्रे प्रीत्या प्रेषयामास हृष्टः ॥१३॥

tatra sthitvā rāghavasyāśrame 'sau
nītvā nāthaḥ pañcaṣān vāsarān saḥ |
jyeṣṭhaṁ tāvac chrī-navadvīpa-bhūmāv
agre prītyā preṣayāmāsa hṛṣṭaḥ ||13||

tatra — there; sthitvā — having stayed; rāghavasya — of Raghava; āśrame — in the abode; asau — He; nītvā — having spent; nāthaḥ — the Master; pañcaṣān — five or six; vāsarān — days; saḥ — He; jyeṣṭham — the senior [companion]; tāvat — meanwhile; śrī-navadvīpa — of Sri Navadvipa; bhūmau — to the land; agre — ahead; prītyā — lovingly; preṣayāmāsa — sent; hṛṣṭaḥ — joyful.

13Having stayed there in Raghava's abode and spent five or six days, the Master, joyful, meanwhile lovingly sent the senior [companion] ahead to the land of Sri Navadvipa.

Note. "The senior" is apparently Paramananda Puri. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 14

तस्मिन् याते गौरचन्द्रः समेतः
श्रीवासस्य प्रेमपात्रस्य गेहम् ।
स्थित्वा तत्र प्राणिमात्रे दयालुः
सर्वत्रासौ संव्यधत्तानुकम्पाम् ॥१४॥

tasmin yāte gauracandraḥ sametaḥ
śrīvāsasya prema-pātrasya geham |
sthitvā tatra prāṇi-mātre dayāluḥ
sarvatrāsau saṁvyadhattānukampām ||14||

tasmin yāte — when he had gone; gauracandraḥ — Gaurachandra; sametaḥ — arrived [with His companions]; śrīvāsasya — of Srivasa; prema — of love; pātrasya — the vessel; geham — at the house; sthitvā — staying; tatra — there; prāṇi-mātre — to every living being; dayāluḥ — compassionate; sarvatra — everywhere; asau — He; saṁvyadhatta — showed; anukampām — mercy.

Note. Metre — vasantatilakā; the verse scans correctly. A chronogram (bhūta-saṅkhyā): the Vedas = 4, the rasas = 6, the shrutis = 4, the moon = 1; the digits are read from right to left — Shaka 1464, i.e. 1542 CE; the month of Ashadha (June–July), a Monday, the second tithi of the dark fortnight. The publisher adds: the Lord appeared in Shaka 1407 and lived forty-seven years; the poem was written nine years after His disappearance; "it is now Shaka 1905, that is, the poem is 498 years old; it has 1911 verses". The publisher's reckoning is inexact: 1407 + 47 = 1454, and from 1454 to 1464 is ten years (according to the Chaitanya-charitamrita, the Lord's disappearance was in Shaka 1455, 1533 CE); 498 = 1905 − 1407, the years since the Lord's appearance, whereas from Shaka 1464 to 1905 is 441 years (?). On the total of 1911 (the printed numbering of the twenty sargas adds up to 1912), see Total verses in the header of the sarga.
